A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GIT/task-tree research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including material relocated or renumbered in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original GIT experiments across graph domains, including fine-tuning, in-context learning, zero-shot evaluation, ablations, and efficiency analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds comparisons with additional graph foundation models and experiments on non-text-attributed graphs.

M1.justification: Section 5.7 introduces an SVD feature-projection module to adapt GIT-G to non-text-attributed graphs. The task-tree construction, encoder aggregation, reconstruction objective, and specialization procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v3 adds non-text-attributed graph coverage: pretraining on PubMed, Citeseer, and IMDB-B, followed by Cora link prediction. This extends the input conditions and introduces IMDB-B while retaining the original text-attributed benchmark coverage.

E2.justification: New Table 3 evaluates GraphPrompt+, All in One, OpenGraph, and AnyGraph across academic, knowledge-graph, and molecular tasks. These four methods were not evaluated in v2, substantially broadening direct comparisons with general graph foundation methods beyond OFA.

E3.justification: Section 5.7 adds a non-text pretraining-to-Cora evaluation protocol using AUC, with three settings varying SVD preprocessing and pretraining. The existing benchmark splits, metrics, training settings, and 500-task few-shot evaluation design are retained.

E4.justification: New Table 6 tests SVD's effect without pretraining and pretraining's effect after SVD, for both GIT-G and GraphMAE. Existing regularizer, specialization, scaling, temporal robustness, and efficiency analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Section 5.1 changes the repetition statement from 'at least five' to 'five' runs with different seeds. Appendix E.1's five-run rule for single-split datasets and existing uncertainty reporting remain unchanged; this does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results are retained after matching renumbered tables. New Table 3 adds four baseline rows below the retained GIT-G domain scores. Table 6 adds non-text Cora results, including AUCs of 95.70 for GIT-G and 95.10 for GraphMAE with SVD and pretraining.

T1.justification: The task-tree definitions, assumptions, Theorems 3.1, 3.3, and 3.5, and their Appendix D proofs are unchanged. Revisions to the theoretical section's introduction and heading do not alter its mathematics.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the central contributions: task-trees unify graph tasks, theoretical analysis supports transfer, and GIT enables general pretraining and domain specialization across roughly 32 graphs and five domains. The rewritten abstract and contribution list preserve this scope.

C2.justification: Section 5.7 interprets the new experiment as evidence that GIT-G applies beyond textual attributes, addressing a direction previously discussed as future work. The limitations concerning information loss and unidentified transferable patterns already appeared in v2 and are largely relocated into the conclusion.

D1.justification: v3 explicitly specifies nearest-prototype inference and documents SVD projection for non-text features. The existing code/data link and Appendix E hyperparameters are retained. Details of the new SVD setup, including its rank, remain unspecified.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations including GraphPrompt, OpenGraph, and AnyGraph, and expands the main-text comparison with GFT in Section 2.3. Since v2 already discussed GFT's relationship in Appendix A, this refines existing positioning rather than introducing an entirely new account.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, task-tree explanations, experimental overview, results discussion, and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting. Section headings are revised, new experimental subsections are inserted, and Appendix B.6's limitations are consolidated into the conclusion.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 3 and 6, adjusts table and caption spacing, and relocates existing displays, including Figures 2 and 4. All ten original figures retain their content; existing tables are chiefly renumbered and repositioned.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens the already extensive empirical evidence with four additional GFM comparators and a controlled non-text experiment, while clarifying the exposition and research positioning. These are useful incremental gains. The non-text evidence remains limited to one downstream evaluation, and the new experiments receive relatively sparse configuration and uncertainty detail.
